findings: Num 15:39, numbers_15_37_to_41.xml (he): the source prints a meteg under the ayin of עֵינֵיכֶם, but the XML has none. Above the khaf are two dots stacked vertically. That is zaqef qatan, not a single stress dot. The source reads עֵֽינֵיכֶ֔ם; the XML has עֵינֵיכֶ֔ם.

Num 15:41, first אלהיכם (he): there is a single dot above the khaf, which is revia; it is correctly encoded. A short vertical stroke stands just left of the hataf segol under the alef. I read it as meteg, giving אֱֽלֹהֵיכֶ֗ם. The XML has none.

Num 15:40 לאלהיכם (he): there is a vertical stroke inside the word that is not the silluq, so a meteg is present. At this crop scale I cannot tell whether it belongs to the first lamed (tsere) or the second lamed (holam). See pending_human.

Pronunciation rubric (index.xml line 199; expanded index line 790): the verb is printed as four Rashi-script glyphs, and the last one descends like a final pe. That rules out the five-letter לגרוס. The encoded לצרף is accepted. אכן is correct, because the first glyph is the Rashi alef, which looks like ח and has no lamed ascender. The defective רוח is retained, correctly, with no sic/corr.

findings: barekhu.xml (he): Psalm 113:2 (and ברוך שם) sit inside the scope of prayer-part barekhu/yitbarakh. The terminator comes only after Psalm 113:2. So any transclusion of barekhu/yitbarakh carries Psalm 113:2 with it (see expanded_order).

index.xml (he) line 194 and expanded index line 785: בלחש is encoded as tei:note type=instruction. It says how the next passage is said, which JLPTEI-3 'Kinds of rubric' classes as a description. It should be type=description, placed first inside the passage's scope.

el_melekh_neeman.xml: יחיד אומר is a when-rubric: it says the text is said by a person praying alone, i.e. without a minyan. Per 'Kinds of rubric' it should be the j:conditional's own tei:note type=instruction, not a description inside the scope. The inverse minyan=false condition itself is correct.

shema_yisrael.xml (he): the enlarged single letters ע and ד use tei:hi rend=large. JLPTEI-3 reserves tei:hi for words and assigns single characters to tei:c rend=large. I did not confirm in the ODD that tei:c is allowed here.

Header idno: numbers_15_37_to_41.xml, deuteronomy_6_5_to_9.xml and deuteronomy_11_13_to_21.xml, in both languages, give whole-chapter URNs (bible:numbers/15, deuteronomy/6, deuteronomy/11) for excerpts. The milestones themselves are correct: a numbered chapter without corresp, verse corresp, bare terminators. The header nonetheless over-claims and should name the verse range.

The three Shema Bible-paragraph files have no liturgical identity and no tei:seg source, while shema_yisrael uses seg source plus prayer:shema/*. Whether vehavta/vehayah/vayomer need prayer:shema/* context URNs should be decided against the registry. I did not check the registry.

Correct as encoded: quotations in emet_veemunah and barekhu carry tei:seg source with chapter/verse milestones nested inside prayer-part scope and terminated explicitly; citation notes carry no parentheses; the role notes have no rend and use the correct xml:lang (yi labels, he קו״ח with abbr/expan קהל וחזן); each verse has exactly one milestone across page breaks (Deut 6:6, 6:7 and Num 15:39 straddle pb); facs follow sN = IA n(N-1) (s18 n17, s19 n18, s20 n19, s21 n20, s22 n21, s23 n22); pb/@n holds the printed page labels 12–14.

Each of the 20 Shema verses has exactly one milestone in Hebrew and one in English, with identical corresp: Deut 6:4–9 (6), 11:13–21 (9), Num 15:37–41 (5). English partial-verse continuations (11:13 comma, 11:20 comma, 6:7 across pb, 15:39 across pb) do not shift any boundary.

The prayer-part milestones for Barekhu (call/response/yitbarakh), Maariv Aravim (opening/seal) and Emet (opening, mosheh, mi_khamokhah, malkhutekha, yimlokh, seal) match across the two languages and are independent of the printed paragraphs. The untranslated Psalm 113:2 sits inside the shared yitbarakh segment and creates no drift.

The call → yitbarakh → response order follows the concurrent columns: the congregation column starts level with the call. This is a reasonable reading and not a Birnbaum import. But the source does not say 'during'. The column also runs alongside the response and the start of Maariv Aravim, so the order remains an interpretation.

Because barekhu/yitbarakh extends through Psalm 113:2, the expanded order puts Psalm 113:2 (and ברוך שם) inside the minyan gate and before the response. That conflicts with the requirement that Psalm 113:2 has no intrinsic minyan gate.

El melekh ne'eman is gated on the inverse condition: correct. The Maariv settings are declared and ended locally: correct. The morning section declares maariv false and selects existing morning material: correct. No three-word Shema repetition has been invented. The installment ends at גאל ישראל, Hashkivenu is absent, and the editions are marked DRAFT/in progress. Nothing here certifies the whole service as complete.
The verse ranges deuteronomy/6/5-/6/9, 11/13-/11/21 and numbers/15/37-/15/41 (documentary) and target/targetEnd (expanded) are complete and terminated.
The barekhu/yitbarakh scope is too wide (see above). Only the header chapter idnos over-claim; the milestone scopes do not.
